$description: Struct-level golden vectors for postFieldBytes — the post id and PoW preimage (TYPES_INTERFACE -> Layout - Post). RESET at Phase 2: these bytes are the positional dialect, not the fixed-width-LE one, and every post id in the system moved with them. The encode direction runs the production writer; the decode direction runs an independent reader written from the layout table, so a vector also proves the preimage is self-delimiting and canonical.

vectors.name: post/minimal
vectors.note: 68 bytes: 1 + 0 content, 32 author, 1 count, 32 challenge, 1 version, 1 timestamp. The struct's own shape, with every field at its zero value — so the byte COUNT is what this pins, and nothing else can.

vectors.name: post/golden
vectors.note: 132 bytes, and THE cross-implementation anchor: the demo UI's hand-written mirror is asserted byte-identical to it. Adjacent fields hold distinct non-zero values (author 00..1f, ref 11.., challenge 20..3f), because an all-zeros vector cannot detect a field-order swap and field order IS the specification. One parent ref, not two: MAX_PARENT_REFS is 1.

vectors.name: post/no-refs
vectors.note: post/golden with the ref removed: exactly 32 bytes shorter. That delta is the dialect change with the largest byte impact — a ref used to cost u32LE(64) + the 64 characters of its hex TEXT, 68 bytes, and now costs the 32 raw bytes it names.

vectors.name: post/wide-numerics
vectors.note: Both vlqU fields at MAX_SAFE_INTEGER — eight bytes each, the top of the encodable number domain. One byte more and readVlqU raises vlq-overflow, which is exactly what keeps the ten-byte all-ones sentinel from ever decoding back into a plausible value.

vectors.name: post/multibyte-content
vectors.note: lpUtf8 counts BYTES, not characters: 11 characters encode as 0x12 = 18 bytes. Two refs so the array's count byte is not stuck at 0 or 1 (the ENCODER has no cap — MAX_PARENT_REFS is a validation rule, and putting it inside the writer would be a guard added to compensate for a domain, which the format forbids). timestamp 128 is the two-byte VLQ boundary.

rejects.name: post/non-minimal-content-length
rejects.note: post/minimal with the content length written as the padded `80 00` instead of `00`. Decodes to a byte-identical value, so steps 1 and 2 both pass and only the re-encode compare separates it.

rejects.name: post/trailing-byte
rejects.note: post/minimal with one byte appended. The struct is fully satisfied before the input runs out — step 2.

rejects.name: post/truncated-author
rejects.note: Empty content and then 19 of the author's 32 bytes. Wire's own rejection, not a boundary-check one: a fixed-width read that runs off the end.

rejects.name: post/timestamp-past-safe-integer
rejects.note: The timestamp written as u64-max — the ten bytes a malformed number field takes on the ENCODE side. It must not decode back into anything, which is the property that makes the sentinel unreachable from a well-formed post rather than merely unlikely.
